course_name_original: Grundlagen des Gründens – Selbstständigkeit und Unternehmertum
course_name_en: Fundamentals of Founding – Self-Employment and Entrepreneurship
prerequisites: Basic knowledge of development methods of one's own discipline

learning_outcomes.text: Students can perceive, name, and discuss business problem areas and potentials of their own entrepreneurship. They can constructively name individual competencies and deficits within the framework of interdisciplinary collaborations.

Students are able to constructively apply their acquired knowledge of risk and potential analysis to the iterative creation of business models for their own start-ups. They can efficiently and results-orientedly plan and deploy competencies within the framework of interdisciplinary collaborations.
Students can evaluate business and legal potentials and risks of entrepreneurial action and, after a positive evaluation, apply methods for creating business models.
Students are able to design a business model for a project developed during their studies in an interdisciplinary network, specifically using the Business Model Canvas and/or the Blue Ocean strategy.
Students create innovative business models by applying their didactic and methodical repertoire in a target-group-oriented manner and appropriate to the application case.

Students are able to present business models in writing as part of applications and rhetorically in a target-group-oriented and convincing manner. In interdisciplinary start-ups, they can define communicative problem areas and apply various solution strategies for them.
Students are able to fulfill their social responsibility and responsibility for themselves as entrepreneurs through continuous evaluation of individual actions.

syllabus_topics: Theoretical foundations of the business, legal and planning requirements for entrepreneurial founding (by interdisciplinary working groups)
Reading, understanding and creating business plans for entrepreneurial start-ups
Practical foundations of interdisciplinary communication in the context of entrepreneurial founding
assessment_rules: The ungraded experimental work serves as the basis for the graded project report. The result of the experimental work is described in the project report and presented in a presentation. The project report should be approximately 15 pages and include illustrative, photographic, or filmic representations. The experimental work is a design activity lasting approximately 3 months from the context of the course.
bibliography: Alexander Osterwalder, Business Model Generation, Campus Verlag, 2011
Eric Ries: Lean Startup: Schnell, risikolos und erfolgreich Unternehmen gründen, Redline Verlag, 2012
Patrick Stähler: Das Richtige gründen. Werkzeugkasten für Unternehmer, Murmann Verlag, 2017
W. Chan Kim: Der Blaue Ozean als Strategie, Carl Hanser Verlag, 2005
